# Pickroute (formerly CS2 IP Changer)

> Free Windows app (Windows 10 and 11, 64-bit) for Counter-Strike 2 that routes CS2 and Steam through a phone's mobile data (Android or iPhone), so community servers see the carrier's IP and not the player's home IP. It keeps the home IP out of community server logs and ban lists without a VPN (servers see an ordinary mobile connection, so it usually gets in where anti-VPN plugins block VPNs), and after an IP ban on a community server the player changes IP from the app and joins again. It is not a VPN and does not touch the game process, its memory or its program files.

Website: https://sepd0x.github.io/cs2-ip-changer/
The same pages in Brazilian Portuguese, Spanish (Latin America), Russian and Turkish: https://sepd0x.github.io/cs2-ip-changer/pt-br/, https://sepd0x.github.io/cs2-ip-changer/es/, https://sepd0x.github.io/cs2-ip-changer/ru/, https://sepd0x.github.io/cs2-ip-changer/tr/ (the app is in English, Brazilian Portuguese, Spanish, Russian and Turkish)
Source and downloads: https://github.com/Sepd0x/cs2-ip-changer (latest release: https://github.com/Sepd0x/cs2-ip-changer/releases/latest)
Download: https://github.com/Sepd0x/cs2-ip-changer/releases/latest/download/CS2IPChanger.exe (CS2IPChanger.exe, 63.9 MB, SHA-256 99bc77fa3778afdd315896f5dd12d476f98536f84733cf2d85773fd111019cfb, VirusTotal: 1 of 67 engines flag it, https://www.virustotal.com/gui/file/99bc77fa3778afdd315896f5dd12d476f98536f84733cf2d85773fd111019cfb/detection)
Status: stable. Latest release 1.0.0 (2026-11-27). Free, no account. Not affiliated with Valve.

## What people use it for

- Keep the home IP private on CS2 community servers: admins and their plugins see the carrier's IP, so the home IP is not in their logs and can't be banned or targeted.
- CS2 server picker / region picker: choose which regions CS2 matchmaking (Premier, Competitive, Casual, Deathmatch, Wingman) can use, with the ping of each region. Works without the phone. The same for Dota 2 and Deadlock, each game with its own regions.
- A new IP after an IP ban on a community server, without a VPN (community servers often block VPN and datacenter IPs).
- Steam account switcher for players with several accounts, with ban and cooldown status.
- Copy CS2 settings (binds, crosshair, video) between Steam accounts.

## Short answers

- What is Pickroute? Pickroute (formerly CS2 IP Changer) is a free Windows app that sends CS2 and Steam through a phone's mobile data, so community servers see the carrier's IP and not the home IP. It also has a CS2 region picker, a Steam account switcher, a CS2 config manager and a Steam profile editor.
- Is there a CS2 server picker that still works in 2026? Yes, several. They all block Valve's relays (Steam Datagram Relay) for the regions you don't want with Windows Firewall rules. Pickroute's Regions page does it with one rule for cs2.exe only and shows the ping of each region; Server Picker X (FN-FAL113) also runs on Linux. Comparison: https://sepd0x.github.io/cs2-ip-changer/cs2-region-picker/#cs2-server-pickers-compared
- How do you change region in CS2? CS2 has no region setting. Block the regions you don't want (a server picker does this) and matchmaking only finds matches in the regions left.
- Is a CS2 server picker safe? It adds Windows Firewall rules and does not touch the game, its files or its memory. Nobody but Valve can promise how Valve treats it.
- Does CS2 IP ban? Valve does not: VAC bans, game bans and cooldowns are on the Steam account. Community servers can ban a SteamID, an IP or an IP range.
- Is a VAC ban an IP ban? No. It is on the Steam account. A new IP does not lift it.
- How can a player hide their home IP from a CS2 community server without a VPN? By playing through a phone's mobile data (USB tethering or hotspot): the server sees the carrier's IP. Pickroute sends only the game through the phone and blocks it on the home connection.
- Can you play CS2 on a phone hotspot? Yes, with a higher ping than on a home line. Valve gives no official data figure; players report roughly 150 to 450 MB an hour.
- Is it a cheat? No. It does not read or change the game and does not hide anything from VAC or any anti-cheat.
- Does it work with an iPhone? Yes. A new IP on an iPhone comes from switching Airplane Mode on and off.

## How it works

- The phone shares its mobile data with the PC over USB tethering or its Wi-Fi hotspot. A 4G/5G USB dongle or router also works as the connection.
- The app adds Windows routes so CS2, Steam and the servers on the user's list go through the phone, and blocks them on the home connection. The browser, Discord and downloads stay on the home connection (Game only mode). The whole PC can go through the phone instead.
- Kill switch (shown in the app's Checks as "Block if the phone drops"): a Windows Firewall rule blocks the listed servers on every adapter except the phone, and cs2.exe's game traffic (UDP) can only use the phone connection. If the cable comes out, the game loses connection instead of falling back to the home IP. Until a phone has been connected once, CS2 is not locked, and in No phone mode nothing is blocked.
- Change IP: turns mobile data (or airplane mode) off and on over ADB until the carrier gives a new IP. It can report whether the new IP is in a new /16 range and keep trying until it is.
- Needs admin rights (routes and firewall rules are system settings), Windows Firewall on, and an Android phone or iPhone with mobile data. Changing IP from the PC needs Android with USB debugging; on an iPhone the player switches Airplane Mode on and off.

## Features

- Change IP and rejoin after a kick or an IP ban, also from inside the game with a hotkey (Ctrl+Shift+F10 by default). After a ban it also logs into the next Steam account that server hasn't banned.
- Live checks of Windows Firewall, routes, the IP servers see next to the home IP, whether the phone is really on mobile data and whether Steam uses the same connection as the game, plus a leak test.
- Connection quality: ping, jitter and loss through the phone every 30 seconds.
- Server list from IP:port or steam://connect links with name, map, players and ping; can wait for a slot on a full server.
- Steam account switcher for alt accounts: uses the logins Steam already saved, switching never asks for passwords (only the optional Profiles sign-in does, and it keeps an encrypted sign-in token, never the password); shows VAC, game and trade bans and cooldowns; marks server bans per account and community. New IP + next account (Ctrl+Shift+F9) gets a new IP, logs into the next account in rotation and rejoins the last server.
- CS2 config manager: copies binds, crosshair, game settings, video and HUD/radar/audio between accounts, with backups, snapshots and compare.
- Profiles: changes the Steam name, picture, bio, country, privacy and custom URL of chosen accounts from templates, with preview and restore.
- Regions: picks where CS2, Dota 2 or Deadlock matchmaking can put the player, on one dial (a spoke per region, its length the ping) and a list by continent; turned-off regions are blocked by one Windows Firewall rule for the game's exe on Valve's relay IPs only. Presets save a set of regions by name, and one can apply by itself when CS2 starts.
- Phone setup: steps for the cable, USB driver, USB debugging, tethering and the phone's Wi-Fi that check themselves (green or red), with a button where the app can do the step.
- Protection starts off each time the app opens; Turn on protection (on the Connection page or the tray icon) turns it on until you turn it off.
- No phone mode: play on the home connection (not protected) while accounts, configs, profiles and regions keep working.

## What it is not

- Not a VPN or proxy: servers see an ordinary mobile connection from the player's carrier, so it usually gets in on community servers whose anti-VPN plugins block VPN and datacenter IPs. Not guaranteed: carriers share mobile IPs, so one can be flagged, and Change IP gets another.
- Not a cheat and no VAC bypass: it does not hide cheats from any anti-cheat. A ban on a Steam account follows the account; a new IP does not lift it.
- Will ping be worse? Usually, yes: mobile data adds latency and jitter compared with a home connection.
- Who sees the IP: on community servers joined directly, the server admins and their plugins. Official matchmaking goes through Valve's relays (Steam Datagram Relay).

## Guides

- [Change IP with your phone](https://sepd0x.github.io/cs2-ip-changer/change-ip-with-phone/): setup from start to finish, game-only routing and a new IP in one click.
- [CS2 with an iPhone](https://sepd0x.github.io/cs2-ip-changer/cs2-iphone-hotspot/): the protection works the same with an iPhone (Personal Hotspot by USB or Wi-Fi); for a new IP the player switches Airplane Mode on and off on the iPhone.
- [CS2 on mobile data](https://sepd0x.github.io/cs2-ip-changer/cs2-mobile-data/): playing CS2 on a phone hotspot or USB tethering, the ping to expect, how much data a match uses and how to keep it steady.
- [CS2 IP ban](https://sepd0x.github.io/cs2-ip-changer/cs2-ip-ban/): does CS2 IP ban, is a VAC ban an IP ban, which ban you have (IP, range, SteamID or Valve) and how to get back in.
- [Hide your IP without a VPN](https://sepd0x.github.io/cs2-ip-changer/hide-ip-cs2/): who sees your IP, what they can do with it, and every method compared.
- [Is it safe?](https://sepd0x.github.io/cs2-ip-changer/is-it-safe/): what it changes and how to check the download.
- [Steam account switcher](https://sepd0x.github.io/cs2-ip-changer/steam-account-switcher/): no passwords, ban marks per server.
- [Copy CS2 settings](https://sepd0x.github.io/cs2-ip-changer/copy-cs2-config/): crosshair, binds and video on every account.
- [CS2 server picker and region picker](https://sepd0x.github.io/cs2-ip-changer/cs2-region-picker/): how to change your region in CS2 (CS2 has no region setting), step by step, the CS2 server pickers compared (Server Picker X, CS2 Server Picker, CS2 Region Picker, CS2 MM Server Picker), and how to do the same block by hand with Windows Firewall.
- [Steam profile editor](https://sepd0x.github.io/cs2-ip-changer/steam-profile-editor/): name, avatar and privacy on many accounts.
- [CS2 ping test](https://sepd0x.github.io/cs2-ip-changer/cs2-ping-test/): how to test your ping to every Valve matchmaking region before you queue, what a good ping is (a rule of thumb) and what to do about spikes.
- [CS2 config file location](https://sepd0x.github.io/cs2-ip-changer/cs2-config-file-location/): where CS2 saves your config on Windows (Steam\userdata\<account ID>\730\local\cfg), what each file holds, where autoexec.cfg goes and how to back it up.
- [CS2 server picker not working](https://sepd0x.github.io/cs2-ip-changer/cs2-server-picker-not-working/): what to check, in order, when a CS2 server picker blocks nothing or you still land in a blocked region: Windows Firewall on for the active profile (some antivirus suites replace it), CS2 restarted after the change, Max Acceptable Matchmaking Ping, a rule for another cs2.exe, an old relay list, and Valve sending a match through a relay you allowed (no picker can stop that).
- [Dota 2 and Deadlock region picker](https://sepd0x.github.io/cs2-ip-changer/dota-2-deadlock-region-picker/): the Regions page also picks the matchmaking regions of Dota 2 (app 570, dota2.exe) and Deadlock (app 1422450, deadlock.exe), each game with its own regions, ping, presets and Windows Firewall rule.

## Safety and privacy

- Releases are built by GitHub Actions from the public source, with a build attestation and a SHA-256 file.
- Updates install only if the SHA-256 matches and is signed with the project's offline key, which is not on GitHub.
- The exe is not code-signed, so Windows SmartScreen warns the first time.
- Usage stats, on by default: the first start shows what is sent, with Accept and Turn off, and Settings > Send usage stats turns them off any time (nothing is sent then, and the app works the same). When the app has been open for 20 seconds, every 30 minutes while it stays open (if something new was counted) and when it closes, plus a short signal every 5 minutes of what is on, with a random ID made for this install, with no name, never from the PC or the user (Delete my stats in Settings deletes it all): versions, country, mode, how the phone is connected, minutes open, button counts, a few counters, list sizes and errors. Nothing is sent and no ID is made before you answer. Never IPs, servers, accounts or names; the server stores no IP.
- Save bug report saves a .zip on the Desktop and sends nothing. It leaves out the current and last home IP, API key, logins, names, SteamIDs, e-mails, Wi-Fi names and the Windows user.
- Third parties: ipwho.is receives the home IP and the phone's IP when the app shows their carrier and city (each asked only through its own connection); ipify, icanhazip, Amazon and Cloudflare see the IP they measure; Steam, Google (ADB download) and GitHub (updates) get normal requests.
- It never opens CS2's memory and never injects into the game: it changes Windows routes and firewall rules, and which Steam account logs in.
